accepted.question_text: Let W be the Coxeter group from the paper, let H be its Iwahori-Hecke algebra over A = Z[v, v^{-1}] with standard basis {T_w ; w in W}, and define structure constants f_{x,y,z} in A by T_x T_y = sum_{z in W} f_{x,y,z} T_z. Is there an integer N >= 0 such that for every x, y, z in W, the shifted coefficient v^{-N} f_{x,y,z} lies in Z[v^{-1}]?

evidence.quote: For x, y, z in W we define fx,y,z ∈ A, hx,y,z ∈ A by TxTy = P z∈W fx,y,zTz, cxcy = P z∈W hx,y,zcz.
(b) Show that there exists an integer N ≥ 0 such that for any x, y, z in W we have v−N fx,y,z ∈ Z[v−1].

accepted.question_text: Assume the boundedness statement in problem (b): there is an integer N >= 0 such that v^{-N} h_{x,y,z} is in Z[v^{-1}] for all x, y, z in W, where the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis elements satisfy c_x c_y = sum_{z in W} h_{x,y,z} c_z. For each z in W, let a(z) be the unique integer such that every h_{x,y,z} lies in v^{a(z)} Z[v^{-1}] and for some x, y the coefficient h_{x,y,z} does not lie in v^{a(z)-1} Z[v^{-1}]. Then define integers gamma_{x,y,z^{-1}} by h_{x,y,z} = gamma_{x,y,z^{-1}} v^{a(z)} mod v^{a(z)-1} Z[v^{-1}], let J be the free abelian group with basis {t_w ; w in W}, and define multiplication by t_x t_y = sum_{z in W} gamma_{x,y,z^{-1}} t_z. Does this multiplication always define an associative ring structure on J, even when J has no unit in general?
accepted.context_brief: Associativity of the asymptotic Hecke algebra

evidence.quote: We will now assume that (b) holds. With N as in (b), we see that v−N hx,y,z ∈ Z[v−1] for any x, y, z in W. It follows that for any z ∈ W there is a unique integer a(z) ≥ 0 such that hx,y,z ∈ v a(z)Z[v−1] for all x, y in W and hx,y,z ∉/ v a(z)−1Z[v−1] for some x, y in W. Hence for x, y, z in W there is a well defined integer γx,y,z−1 such that hx,y,z = γx,y,z−1 v a(z) mod v a(z)−1Z[v−1]. Let J be the free abelian group with basis {tw; w ∈ W}. For x, y in W we set txty = P z∈W γx,y,z−1 tz.
(c) Show that this defines an (associative) ring structure on J (without 1 in general).

accepted.question_text: Let W be a finite Weyl group with L = ||, let C be a conjugacy class in W, and let C_min be the subset of elements of C having minimal length. For w in C, define N^w in A = Z[v, v^{-1}] to be the trace of the A-linear map H -> H given by h -> v^{2|w|} T_w h T_{w^{-1}}, where H is the Iwahori-Hecke algebra of W. For w in C_min, the paper states that N^w depends only on C, and it calls C positive when N^w belongs to N[v^2]. Determine all positive conjugacy classes when W is a Weyl group of type B_n or D_n.
accepted.context_brief: Positive conjugacy classes in types B_n and D_n

evidence.quote: (a) Show that the algebras associated in [S20] to a supercuspidal representation of a parabolic subgroup of a p-adic reductive group are (up to extension by a group algebra of a small finite group) of the form Hq where q is a power of p, with H associated to an affine Weyl group W and with L in the collection ΣW of weight functions on W described in [L91, §17], [L95], [L02].

For example, if W is of affine type F4, then ΣW consists of all L whose values on {si; i ∈ I} are (1, 1, 1, 1, 1) or (1, 1, 1, 2, 2) or (2, 2, 2, 1, 1) or (1, 1, 1, 4, 4); if W is of affine type G2, then ΣW consists of all L whose values on {si; i ∈ I} are (1, 1, 1) or (1, 1, 3) or (3, 3, 1) or (1, 1, 9).
